pr_title: [Mono] Restore old code to solve the recent SpanHelpers regressions
pr_body:
Fixes #75709

As discovered in #dotnet/perf-autofiling-issues#7976 (and #74395), SpanHelpers vectorization work in #73768 that went into RC1 caused severe Span.IndexOf performance regressions on mono. This PR restores the previous implementation for mono while retaining the performance gains seen for coreclr.

This is a temporary workaround for the regression on mono, but .NET 7.0 will ship with this workaround in place. For .NET 8, we have #75801 to explore the better long-term resolution.

This PR does not include the changes introduced in the following PRs:

#73481 (it caused the JSON comment parsing regression: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/74442)
#73368 and #73469 where I've removed `AdvSimd.Arm64` code-path and started using Vector128/256 everywhere. The reason for that is WASM/Mono does not support Vector128/256 for all configs (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73469#discussion_r943948656), so I've not included these changes.

- [x] ensure the CI is green for all the configs
- [ ] verify the performance for Mono AOT and WASM

cc @jkotas @vargaz

issue_context.title: [wasm] Perf regression of Span.IndexOf
issue_context.body:
The performance of `Span`'s `IndexOf` got worse with https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73768 on wasm.

Visible in https://github.com/dotnet/perf-autofiling-issues/issues/7981, https://github.com/dotnet/perf-autofiling-issues/issues/7976 and here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4147484/190492419-3a08febd-38d0-4b55-88b5-6bfaf1575a50.png)

I think what is happening is that after the change we end up calling a shared generic method in the span helper, instead of an inflated one.

Stack trace before:
```
$corlib_System_SpanHelpers_IndexOf_byte__byte_int (dotnet.wasm:0x64acc)
$Wasm_Browser_Bench_Sample_Sample_SpanTask_IndexOfByte_RunStep (dotnet.wasm:0x4bddf0)
invoke_vii (dotnet.js:7557)
$Wasm_Browser_Bench_Sample_BenchTask_Measurement__RunBatchd__13_MoveNext (dotnet.wasm:0x4c0162)
...
```
after:
```
$corlib_System_SpanHelpers_IndexOfValueType_TValue_BYTE_TNegator_INST_TValue_BYTE__TValue_BYTE_int (dotnet.wasm:0x66aca)
$Wasm_Browser_Bench_Sample_Sample_SpanTask_IndexOfByte_RunStep (dotnet.wasm:0x4f9be2)
invoke_vii (dotnet.js:7557)
$Wasm_Browser_Bench_Sample_BenchTask_Measurement__RunBatchd__13_MoveNext (dotnet.wasm:0x4fbf53)
...
```

review_comments: Shouldn't this one be also behind `#if !MONO`?
I think you're right, @radekdoulik. This set of overloads wasn't resurrected into `.Mono.cs`, but it's the only of these IndexOf methods still using `where T : struct, INumber<T>` on mono.
I would place these under `#if !MONO` instead. ifdefs are fine as temporary workarounds, and it will make it easy to see that there is no change for !MONO.
I assume that this is copy&paste without any changes.

That's my understanding. But I'm trying to make sure I understand the point in history from which it was all copied. @adamsitnik or I will circle back here to edit the description to include notes pointing to the source of the copy.
